evaluator: Independent Codex reviewer using a fictionalized Margaret Morse analytical lens; not Margaret Morse and no endorsement implied.
evidence: home.png and home.html foreground “Technical Project Manager - Product Operations & Implementation” and provide a visible About link in the primary navigation; one click reaches the required lineage surface while preserving immediate professional role clarity.

about.html explicitly names “Systems people can inhabit,” connects Open House, WOWList, Sunday Dinner / 196, NYC Artist Coalition, and Knowledge Wiki Graphs, and describes the practice as artistic, civic, technical, and social without becoming an artist biography.

about.html supplies a concrete continuity method: observe relationships, model a system, prototype an interface, test it with people, and document enough for others to continue. Its project loops connect that method to commercial operations, coalition work, hospitality, community software, and governed knowledge systems.

wowlist.html shows participation shaping technical form: collaboratively editable natural-language posts, followable keyword communities, organizer-controlled calendars, and distribution workflows grew from the vocabulary and practices of distributed scenes rather than a centralized editorial gatekeeper.

sunday-dinner.html makes hospitality operational without flattening it into administration: invitation, orientation, space configuration, hosting, minimal continuity documentation, follow-up, and resident-artist agency are presented as repeatable systems while participant-level records remain withheld.

fair-rent.html states that “The website was one part of the room” and traces a legible sequence across shared public surfaces, facilitated working alignment, public gatherings, source maps, decisions, and follow-through. Its align/translate/implement/sustain model shows how people influence and continue the system.

team-memory.html extends the same lineage into present technical research: knowledge begins in people, language, artifacts, and relationships; semantic, evidence, and source-custody responsibilities remain distinct; corrections and disagreements stay visible; and every public projection requires human review.

work.html and the two-page public-resume.pdf keep the lineage subordinate to an application-ready professional narrative. The work index organizes evidence as operating, civic, community, and knowledge systems, while the resume opens with senior product and technical project management and carries the relevant project continuities into page two.
safety_findings: Collective credit is explicit: WOWList names Richard Caceres as co-founder and co-builder; Sunday Dinner credits its community and identifies Julia Fredenburg as a documented co-organizer; FairRentNYC credits coalition collaborators and repeatedly rejects solo policy causality.

Participant privacy is actively preserved. sunday-dinner.html publishes aggregate scale and redacted workflow form while excluding names, contacts, attendance histories, addresses, access instructions, proposals, correspondence, and unapproved images.

fair-rent.html separates public evidence from private coalition notes, legal-review material, stakeholder lists, raw strategy, and unapproved quotations; it also avoids attributing shared-account posts to individuals or treating public response labels as attendance, endorsement, or impact.

The contemporaneous Open House article contains public quotations and pseudonymized reporting about an unhoused family, but about.html does not repurpose those sensitive details or Margaret Morse’s quotations as promotional testimonial. No protected educational record, private correspondence, or unapproved testimonial projection was observed on the portfolio pages.

team-memory.html clearly states that access is not evidence or publication permission, uses a synthetic worked example instead of a private archive, and denies automated systems publication authority or replacement of human judgment.
recommendation: Pass PR-015 for this individual holdout. Preserve the concise About-page threshold, project-specific privacy boundaries, and collective-credit language; aggregate this score with the other two fresh independent scorecards before applying the rubric’s median requirement or seeking human production approval.
